title: fix: preserve legacy placeholder pseudo-classes
author: maricastroc
summary: Stops parsing `:-moz-placeholder` and `:-ms-input-placeholder` as prefixed `:placeholder-shown` (mapping added in #929, v1.29.3). Those names are the legacy forms of `::placeholder`, so with modern targets the `:is()` lowering prints an unprefixed `:placeholder-shown` copy that styles the whole input in current browsers (Vite 8 report).
evidence: Master (574eee2) --targets 'chrome 111': `a:-ms-input-placeholder, b:-ms-input-placeholder{color:red}` -> `:is(a:-ms-placeholder-shown,b:-ms-placeholder-shown){color:red}:is(a:placeholder-shown,b:placeholder-shown){color:red}`, which changes meaning in a modern browser. Related, not fixed by this PR: prefixing `a:placeholder-shown` for firefox 40 / ie 11 emits non-existent `:-moz-placeholder-shown` / `:-ms-placeholder-shown` (prefixes.rs PseudoClassPlaceholderShown + write_prefixed!); and open #1281 fixes `::-ms-input-placeholder` being rewritten to `::-moz-placeholder` (also reproduced on master). Review could consider handling these together or noting follow-ups. No maintainer comments.
